### TAG-177: Example 12.26 Pure Value Expression of Boolean Full Adder

**Status:** ⬛ Spec only

## Software Notes

**What this example demonstrates:** Example 12.26 shows the *same* full-adder from Example 12.19 rebuilt to terminate in **primitive association relationships** rather than **value transform rules** — a distinction Fant draws explicitly (§12.3.4/12.9): a language expression can properly bottom out either way. Example 12.19's `OR`/`AND`/`NOT` end as lookup tables (`0[1] 1[2]...`, a formed key selecting a stored constant). Example 12.26's versions end instead as sets of tiny minterm-style invocations, of which "only one will achieve completeness of its destination list" — pure wiring, no values being looked up at all. Figure 12.15 shows this concretely: real dual-rail NCL gates (AND/OR/NOT) wired directly, with `A[g,k,o]`-style constructs being plain **fan-out aliases** — content flowing through `A` also flows to `g`, `k`, and `o` simultaneously, via ordinary name correspondence (Fig 12.1b), just written compactly with a bracket-and-comma list instead of repeating the same name three times. Single-target cases (`GI[S]`) are the same mechanism degenerating to a plain wire.

**What we changed in the AST/parser:** No AST changes were needed — `network.Statement.pure_value` (`[]const u8`) already accommodates this; the difference between "a symbolic value" and "a fan-out target list" is purely what the *emitter* eventually does with the content, not something the parser needs to represent structurally. The one parser change: `parseResolution`'s existing bare-token handling gained a new branch — if a bare name is immediately followed by `,` (rather than `<`, `(`, `:`, or `]`), it rewinds and reads the full comma-separated list via `readCommaSeparatedName` (already built for [TAG-136](https://linear.app/taguniversal/issue/TAG-136/example-1245-code-detector-state-machine) 's state-symbol disambiguation), storing the whole thing as one `pure_value`. Existing single-target and numeric-literal forms are unaffected.

**Deliberately out of scope for now:** VHDL emission for fan-out `pure_value` statements is not implemented — this change only makes the syntax parse correctly. Actually wiring a fan-out alias to multiple destinations in generated VHDL is a separate, later task.

## Reference

```
FULLADD($A,$B,$C)(<> CARRYOUT<>)

A[g,k,o] B[h,l,p] C[G,K,O] D[H,L,P] E[I,M,Q] F[J,N,R]
//"define combinational resolution stages"
GI[S] GJ[T] HI[S] HJ[S]

SU[a,c,e] SV[b,d,f] TU[b,d,f] TV[b,d,f] //"fan out input to second half-adder"
ga[i] gb[j] ha[i] hb[i]
kc[m] kd[m] lc[n] ld[m]
oe[q] of[q] pe[q] pf[r]
im[s ] in[ t ] jm[ t ] jn[ t ] //"sum"
qW[u ] qX[ v ] rW[v ] rX[ v ] //"carry"
```
